title: Multiple Offset Cut Lines | Laser Alignment Guide - X Series
body_html:
Cutting Produces Multiple Offset Lines - X Series

Problem Description

During a vector cutting operation, multiple cut lines appear instead of a single, clean line.

Cause

Multiple laser beam paths or scattering issues. This commonly occurs after the laser head sustains an impact or after an optical component in the beam path becomes misaligned:

  • Slight angular deviation in the angle of a mirror.
  • The entire laser head assembly is askew.
  • The focus lens is slightly loose or tilted.

Solution

1. Check if the focus lens is loose. If it is, use the focus lens removal tool (which you can search for and purchase on Amazon) or a thin steel ruler to gently tighten the lens. Be extremely careful not to scratch the lens itself.

2. Place a piece of tape on the third mirror mount of the laser head. Move the laser head to the four corner positions of the working plane (top-left, bottom-left, top-right, and bottom-right), and at each position, tap the Pulse icon on the control panel. Observe the burn marks left on the tape.

  • If the burn marks are not consistent or are off-center, you need to re-align the entire beam path.
  • If the burn marks are centered but the shape of the spot is abnormal, check the focus lens and the nozzle for contamination or damage.

 

Important Reminder:

If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
